name: Lower School
head: Margit Ellery
tagline: Reading corners, gardens and a lot of questions
summary: Pre-K to Grade 5 in the Orchard Building: two teachers in every Pre-K and K room, daily outdoor time and a reading specialist for every grade.
body:
The Lower School sits in the Orchard Building and its walled garden. Children learn to read and count with teachers who know them well, and they spend part of every day outside.

Specialist teachers lead music, art, Spanish, library and physical education from Pre-K. Homework is light and read aloud at home is the main assignment.
day: 8:05~Morning meeting on the rug|8:30~Reading and writing workshop|9:45~Recess in the garden|10:10~Mathematics|11:15~Specials: music, art, Spanish or library|12:00~Lunch and outdoor play|12:50~Quiet reading|1:15~Science or social studies project|2:30~Choice time and clubs|3:05~Dismissal from the Orchard gate
hallmarks: Two teachers in Pre-K and Kindergarten|Daily outdoor learning|Spanish from Pre-K|A reading specialist for every grade|Buddy classes with the Upper School

name: Middle School
head: Daniel Achebe-Ross
tagline: Advisory, the six-day rotation and the first big projects
summary: Grades 6 to 8 in Hollins Hall: daily advisory, the six-day rotation, a choice of language and a Grade 8 capstone presented to families.
body:
Middle School is where students start to run their own week. Every student has an advisor who sees them each morning and checks in with families.

Students move to the six-day rotation, choose Spanish, French or Latin, and join a team or ensemble each season. Grade 8 ends with a capstone project presented to the school.
day: 7:55~Advisory|8:15~Block A or B (rotation)|9:25~Block C|10:30~Break and snack|10:45~Block D|11:50~Lunch and house tables|12:35~Block E|1:40~Block F or study hall|2:40~Athletics, arts or clubs|4:15~Late bus
hallmarks: Daily advisory, 10 students per advisor|Six-day rotation with 70-minute blocks|Spanish, French or Latin|A team or ensemble every season|Grade 8 capstone

name: Upper School
head: Celeste Varga
tagline: Harkness tables, signature courses and the senior thesis
summary: Grades 9 to 12 in the Tarren Building: discussion-based classes at oval tables, signature electives, a senior thesis and college counseling from Grade 10.
body:
Upper School classes meet around oval tables of twelve. Teachers expect students to read, argue and write, and to change their minds when the evidence asks them to.

From Grade 10 each student works with a college counselor. Seniors write and defend a thesis in a subject of their choice.
day: 7:50~Chapel talk or house meeting|8:10~Block A|9:20~Block B|10:25~Community time|10:50~Block C|12:00~Lunch|12:45~Block D|1:55~Block E or free period|3:00~Athletics, arts and rehearsals|5:30~Evening study in the library
hallmarks: Oval-table classes of about 13|Signature courses written by our faculty|College counseling from Grade 10|Senior thesis and defense|Service week every spring
